Fun maths games for kids

Maths at IntelloKids starts with counting objects and comparing sizes for the youngest, moves on to adding up groups of pictures, and builds up to a fast-paced maths race and quizzes with addition, subtraction, multiplication and division for older children. Every correct answer earns stars, and mistakes are recorded so parents know exactly what to practise.

Get started →

🛡️ No ads · No chat with strangers · Parents in control

What your child learns

  • Counting and number sense
  • Comparing: bigger, smaller, more and fewer
  • Addition with pictures, then with numbers
  • Subtraction, multiplication and division for ages 7 to 10
  • Doubles, halves, tens and even numbers in the quizzes

Games your child will play

🔢

Count with Brainy

Ages 3–6

Count the objects one by one and pick the right number.

🔗

Connect the dots

Ages 3–10

Tap the numbers in order; older children count in 2s or 5s.

🐘

Big and small

Ages 3–6

Compare sizes and tap the big or the small one.

➕

Adding up

Ages 5–10

Add up groups of pictures to find the total.

🕒

Tell the time

Ages 5–10

Read the clock: o’clock, half past and quarter past or to.

🏁

Maths race

Ages 7–10

Answer quick sums to make the airplane fly.

❓

Quiz

Ages 3–10

Short, mixed quizzes, and a big quiz at the end of every world.

Questions parents ask

At what age can my child start the maths games?

From 3. The youngest children count and compare, 5 and 6 year olds add up with pictures, and 7 to 10 year olds practise all four operations in the maths race and the quizzes.

Do the maths games follow the school curriculum?

They practise the core early-maths skills taught in primary school, such as counting, number order, addition, subtraction and multiplication, in a playful way. They complement school learning rather than replace it.
